resources.string: Expands by itself from the pattern: %1$s

A pattern lets one snippet take a different piece of text each time. Give the snippet the pattern ^hello (.+)$ and the text \"Hello, $1! Nice to meet you.\" Then type \"hello John\" and a space, and the keyboard writes \"Hello, John! Nice to meet you.\" Use $1 to $9 for each part in brackets, and ${1:upper}, ${1:lower}, ${1:title} or ${1:trim} to change one. One backspace puts back what you typed.

How many snippet tiles sit side by side in the keyboard\'s panel
Let a trigger you type turn into its snippet inside a password box

Off by default. With it on, pressing space or Enter in a password field, or typing the symbol a trigger ends in, makes the keyboard read back the few characters before the cursor and check them against your triggers. Nothing it reads is learned, kept or sent. The space that ends a trigger is not typed into the password; Enter still does what the field asks. Patterns, chips that ask first and apps typing snippets through automation stay off in password fields, and number-only PIN fields are not covered.
Type it in front of a trigger that expands immediately to keep the trigger as text

A snippet set to expand immediately replaces its trigger as soon as you type the last letter. Type this character just before the trigger and the trigger stays as text. The character itself is removed. The default is a backslash, so \\btw gives btw. Choose Off if you use this character in front of words.
More columns show more snippets at once, which suits short labels. Fewer give each tile more room for its text. Folders use the same grid. The default is 2.
When a snippet has several expansions
What happens after you type the trigger

A snippet can hold more than one text, and can point at other snippets. Chips only: the suggestion bar offers all of them and nothing goes in until you press one. Insert first: the keyboard inserts the default straight away and offers the rest, so pressing one swaps what it put in. Each snippet can answer this on its own.
The suggestion strip offers them all. Nothing goes in until you press one
The default goes in at once. Press another chip to swap it
